text: Board itself, when it senses the physical field, it consumes some power, of course. We have typically CPU, of course, to make it work, and the CPU may, of course, consume power, and then we have the radio interface, right? The radio interface consumes power as well. How much power it depends on what the interface is doing. So if it transmits, you will have the power consumption of the transceiver plus the power that is irradiated, right? The transmit power that we irradiate to transmit the signal. When it receives, is a little bit lower because we only have the power consumption of the transceiver, but we don't have to irradiate any signal we are receiving in that case. When it's idle, if it needs to sense the channel, then it is going to consume, right? Something, and the consumption is essentially the same as the one of the receiver, typically, is comparable. If we put our interface into sleep mode, then of course we are not able to transmit or receive, but the power consumption of the interface will drop significantly. So it is in our interest, in order to save energy power, to put the interface into sleep mode as often as possible. And also, it is of course important not to then consider it as active unless it is necessary.
